tajweed: Reciting every letter correctly, from its point of articulation and with its qualities.
The extra 'n' sound at the end of a noun, written as a doubled vowel mark (ـًـٍـٌ).
Pronouncing the nūn clearly, without merging or nasal hiding.
ء هـ ع ح غ خ — the six letters of iẓhār ḥalqī.
Merging a sākin letter into the next letter so they sound as one stressed letter.
A nasal sound from the nose, held for about two counts.
Changing nūn sākinah or tanwīn into a hidden mīm before the letter bā’ (ب).
Pronouncing the nūn between iẓhār and idghām, hidden, with ghunnah.
Hiding mīm sākinah with ghunnah before bā’ (ب).
Merging mīm sākinah into a following mīm, with ghunnah.
Pronouncing mīm sākinah clearly before all other letters.
The lām of «ال» that is merged into the next letter and not pronounced (الشَّمس).
The lām of «ال» that is pronounced clearly (القَمَر).
Lengthening the sound of a vowel letter (ا و ي).
Basic lengthening of two counts, with no hamzah or sukūn after it.
The unit for measuring the length of a madd.
Madd letter followed by hamzah in the same word; obligatory (wājib).
Madd letter at the end of a word and hamzah at the start of the next; permissible (jā’iz).
Madd letter followed by an original sukūn; held for six counts.
The point of articulation where a letter is produced.
A quality of a letter, such as whispering or strength.
A slight echoing bounce on ق ط ب ج د when they are sākin.
fiqh: Natural water that is pure and can be used for wuḍū’ and ghusl.
Washing specific body parts in a set way before prayer.
An obligatory act; leaving it makes the act of worship invalid.
A recommended act from the Prophet’s ﷺ practice; rewarded, but not obligatory.
The intention in the heart to perform the act of worship.
Things that break wuḍū’, so it must be renewed.
The state of impurity that prevents prayer until one purifies.
Something that must be present before and during the act for it to be valid.
The direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah, faced in prayer.
An essential part inside the prayer; it is invalid without it.
Things that cancel the prayer, so it must be repeated.
Washing the whole body for ritual purity.
Dry ablution using clean earth when water is unavailable or harmful.
Wiping over leather socks worn in purity, instead of washing the feet.
Shortening four-unit prayers to two during travel.
Combining two prayers in the time of one of them, for a valid reason.
shiir: Speech with metre (wazn) and rhyme (qāfiyah) that carries meaning and feeling.
One line of a poem, made of two halves.
The first half of a verse.
The second half of a verse.
The musical rhythm of the verse.
The repeated sound at the end of every verse.
A complete poem with one metre and one rhyme.
One of the famous long pre-Islamic poems.
A short, true saying drawn from life experience.
A poet who lived in both the pre-Islamic era and Islam.
The topic of a poem, such as praise, wisdom or description.
Poetry lamenting loss; in this course, for lost cities.
A historical period of Arabic literature (pre-Islamic, Umayyad, Abbasid…).
imla: Spelling: writing words correctly by the rules.
Written ة; pronounced h when you stop on it.
The wāw meaning ‘they’ on verbs; followed by a written alif (كتبوا).
The -an ending; usually written with an extra alif (كتابًا).
Pronounced only at the start of speech; written as a bare alif (اكتبْ).
Always pronounced; written with a hamzah sign (أكرمَ).
A hamzah in the middle of a word; its seat follows the strongest vowel.
The letter a hamzah sits on: ا, و or ى (ئ).
A hamzah at the end of a word; its seat follows the vowel before it.
A final alif written either as ا or as ى.
A final alif written like yā’ without dots (ى).
nahw: Grammar: rules for the endings and roles of words in a sentence.
A word for a person, thing or idea, without time.
A word for an action linked to time.
A word whose meaning appears only with other words.
Change of a word’s ending according to its role.
Jussive mood for verbs; main sign sukūn (ـْ).
A word whose ending never changes.
A noun that takes no tanwīn and uses fatḥah for jarr.
Two of something; ends in ـان / ـين.
أب، أخ، حم، فو، ذو — marked by letters (و ا ي).
A verb for now or the future; it takes i‘rāb.
The one who does the action; marfū‘.
Replaces the doer in a passive sentence; marfū‘.
The noun a nominal sentence starts with; marfū‘.
What completes the meaning of the mubtada’; marfū‘.
The one the action happens to; manṣūb.
Describes the noun before it and follows its case.
Describes the state of someone at the time of the action; manṣūb.
Clarifies a vague word, such as a number; manṣūb.
arbaeen: A report of what the Prophet ﷺ said, did or approved.
The intention in the heart behind a deed.
Worshipping Allah as though you see Him; He sees you.
Belief in Allah, His angels, books, messengers, the Last Day and the decree.
Something newly introduced into the religion that is not from it.
Things not clearly lawful or unlawful; caution is to avoid them.
Sincere goodwill and counsel — to Allah, His Book, His Messenger, leaders and people.
What the Prophet ﷺ relates from his Lord.
Protecting oneself from Allah’s punishment by obeying Him.
A feeling that holds one back from what is shameful.
Keeping to the straight path of the Sharī‘ah without deviating.
Evidence the claimant must bring in a dispute.
What Allah and His Messenger have forbidden.
Disliking a blessing Allah gave someone else.
Abundant goodness; righteousness is good character.
What troubles the soul and you dislike others to see.
asmaa: Allah’s names, all perfect and beautiful.
Singling out Allah in belief, word and deed.
The perfect Master to whom all turn in their needs.
Allah’s mercy that encompasses all things.
Being mindful that Allah sees and hears you.
Glorifying Allah with heart, tongue and limbs.
Not hastening punishment, giving time to repent.
Stopping, regret, resolve, replacing with good.
Declaring Allah free of every flaw and likeness.
Might of strength, overcoming and invulnerability.
Putting things in their right places.
qul: The form preferred by the best Arabic usage.
Plural patterns for 3–10 items, e.g. أشهر، أبحر.
Word for the one acted upon, e.g. مصون.
The noun of an action, e.g. حيازة.
Af‘al form for comparing, e.g. أفضل.
Making a verb take an object (hamzah or bā’).
After it the verb stays singular: قام الرجلان.
Marking the short vowels to fix meaning.
balagha: Likening two things sharing a quality, with a particle.
The quality the two sides share; stronger in the likened-to.
A simile with its particle stated.
A simile with its particle dropped.
A simile with one side, the particle and the quality dropped.
Only the likened is named; the other is hinted by a trait.
Saying a word and meaning what follows from it; the literal may also be meant.
Joining two words of opposite meaning.
One verb affirmed and negated, or commanded and forbidden.
Several meanings followed by their opposites in order.
Two words alike in sound, different in meaning.
Phrase-endings agreeing in the last letter, in prose.
The last word of a phrase in prose, like rhyme in poetry.
Speech that can be true or false in itself.
Speech that cannot be true or false in itself.
Requesting an action from a position of authority.
A command addressed to an equal.
Seeking to know something not known before.
Asking to identify one of two or more things.
